title: Entitlement Drift Detection & Forensic Readiness Playbook
author: Eleanor Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines the end-to-end detection, alerting, triage, and evidence-packaging processes for entitlement drift (unexpected or unauthorized changes to role bindings, group memberships, service accounts, and temporary elevations). It ties RBAC monitoring to audit logging, data residency constraints, Secure SDLC checkpoints, and incident-response forensics so Redwood can:

- Rapidly detect drift events across control planes (IAM, tenant ACLs, orchestration, model-serving policies).
- Triage and contain drift with minimal blast radius.
- Assemble admissible evidence for legal, compliance, or customer audits while preserving chain-of-custody and residency constraints.

Scope and Audience

This document applies to: production and staging control planes that affect inference access (console, API keys, service identities, feature flags, and model access policies). Primary audience: security operations, SRE, platform engineers, and compliance reviewers.

Definitions

- Entitlement drift: any divergence between an authoritative entitlement state (the desired state recorded in our provisioning system or policy-as-code repo) and the observed effective entitlements in runtime systems.
- Forensic readiness: ability to preserve, collect, and provide trustworthy traces and artifacts to prove what happened and who performed actions.
- Evidence bundle: a time-bound package of logs, snapshots, and metadata used for audits.

Owner & Escalation

- Primary owner: Security Ops (security@redwood.com)
- Secondary owner: Platform SRE (platform-sre@redwood.com)
- Escalation: If drift indicates lateral movement or data exfiltration, escalate immediately to Oncall Security Incident Manager and follow the Incident Response Security runbook (/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/incident-process).

Detection & Alerting Strategy

1) Sources to monitor (examples):
   - IAM change events (cloud provider IAM API): CreateUser, UpdateRole, AttachPolicy, AddRoleBinding
   - Internal entitlement service events: group membership writes, delegated-role activations
   - Service account key lifecycle events: key create/delete, key use from new IP ranges
   - Model-serving access grants: model ACL mutations, tenant-level allowlists
   - Feature-flag activations that enable privileged paths

2) Baseline/authoritative state sources:
   - policy-as-code repo (git): /infra/iam/policies and /platform/entitlements (single source of truth)
   - Provisioning system (Terraform state / config management system)
   - Scheduled inventory snapshots of runtime (every 4 hours)

3) Detection rules and thresholds (examples):
   - High-confidence drift: a direct mismatch between git-authoritative policy and runtime within 10 minutes -> SEV2 alert to Security Ops.
   - Medium confidence: unexpected role binding to a high-privilege role (e.g., "platform-admin", "entitlement-owner") without matching approval ticket -> SEV3 alert.
   - Low confidence: ephemeral group membership mismatch for non-critical roles -> metric alert only (dashboard).

4) Alerting channels: PagerDuty for SEV2/SEV1, Slack #sec-ops for SEV3 triage thread, internal dashboard; all alerts must include: detected_delta, authoritative_reference_commit, first_seen, detected_by_query_id, correlation_id.

Monitoring queries (examples)

- Example SQL (audit-event store):
  SELECT event_time, actor, action, resource, region, request_id
  FROM audit_events
  WHERE action LIKE '%role%'
    AND event_time >= now() - interval '1 hour'
    AND (resource_role IN ('platform-admin','dedicated-operator'))
  ORDER BY event_time DESC;

- Example Kibana DSL for role-binding changes: (description) query on event.type: "iam.change" AND change.target: "role_binding" AND NOT metadata.approved_ticket_id:*

Triage Procedure (quick actions)

1) Acknowledge alert and capture correlation_id.
2) Use the diagnostic checklist:
   - Confirm authoritative state: git commit referenced in alert (git show <commit>).
   - Cross-check provisioning system (terraform state list) for drift markers.
   - Pull audit log slice for event_time +/- 30 minutes and for involved principals.
   - Confirm if change was via automation (pipeline run id, CI actor) or manual (user principal).
3) Contain:
   - If automation error: revert via CI rollback and disable failing pipeline; create a revert PR with emergency tag.
   - If manual and unauthorized: revoke the binding (temporary removal) and rotate any affected credentials. Document change in incident ticket.
4) Escalate:
   - If evidence of compromise (unapproved lateral movement, abnormal artifact access): open Security Incident ticket and follow Incident Response Security playbook.

Forensic Evidence Packaging (evidence bundle spec)

Every evidence bundle MUST include the following artifacts and metadata fields. Keep the bundle representation small (tar.gz encrypted) and signed.

- Mandatory artifacts (minimum):
  - Audit log slice in newline-delimited JSON (event_time window +/- 30m)
  - Snapshot of runtime entitlements (CSV) with SHA256 checksum
  - Git reference: repository, commit SHA, and diff of the authoritative policy
  - Provisioning run logs (Terraform apply outputs, CI pipeline run logs)
  - User/session metadata (IP, geolocation, MFA status) pulled from authn provider
  - S3 object store path or forensic bucket pointer where raw artifacts are kept (encrypted at rest)

- Metadata fields to attach to bundle manifest (JSON):
  - bundle_id (UUID), collected_at (UTC ISO8601), collector, retention_tier, region_residency, legal_hold_flag, chain_of_custody (list of actions + actor + timestamp)

- Evidence signature and storage:
  - Sign the bundle with Redwood evidence signing key (KMS key alias: alias/redwood/evidence-signing).
  - Store hot copy minimum 90 days in encrypted forensic S3 bucket (s3://forensics-<region>) with server-side KMS. Cold archive copies moved to WORM storage with 7-year retention where applicable by regulation.

Data Residency & Retention Considerations

- Residency mapping: Each artifact must be labeled with region_residency based on the source system (us-west-2, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1). The collector must not move raw PII-containing logs outside their original region unless explicitly permitted.
- Retention policy (default):
  - Hot (fast access): 90 days (for triage and operational forensics)
  - Warm: additional 275 days (total 365 days) for compliance queries
  - Cold/Archive: up to 7 years where required by contract/regulation; otherwise 2 years.
- Deletion/Legal hold: Legal hold flags block retention transitions. Deletion requires: security approval, legal approval, and completion of evidence manifest.

Chain of Custody and Auditability

- Every evidence action (collect, transfer, sign, export) must be recorded in the evidence manifest and in the centralized audit store with following fields: action, actor, timestamp, target_object, justification_ticket.
- Evidence manifests are themselves logged to the immutable-audit-store topic and have unique evidence_id that maps back to the incident ticket.

Integration with Secure SDLC & Model Onboarding

- Preventative controls:
  - All policy changes must pass policy-as-code checks in CI (static analysis rules for least-privilege, role naming conventions, and residency tags).
  - Any change to high-privilege roles requires two approvers and a dedicated release gate in the deployment pipeline.
- Gate validation artifacts: The Secure SDLC gate produces an artifact (gate_proof.json) that must be attached to any evidence bundle created within 72 hours of that gate activation.

Operational Playbook: Step-by-step (fast response)

1) Detect -> page Security Ops with SEV code.
2) Acknowledge & gather: run quick-collection script: ./ops/collect-entitlement-slice.sh --ticket=<id> --window=30m --out=/tmp/evidence-<id>.tgz
3) Reproduce assertion: compare the collected entitlements CSV with git-authoritative CSV: ./tools/compare-entitlements --gold=repo/authoritative.csv --observed=/tmp/entitlements.csv
4) Contain: revoke binding using least-disruptive step (example CLI):
   - gcloud iam roles remove-binding --role=roles/platformAdmin --member=user:jane@redwood.com --project=redwood-prod
   - or internal: rbackctl revoke --binding-id=<binding> --reason="unapproved-drift"
5) Package evidence: run ./ops/package-evidence.sh --input=/tmp/evidence-<id> --kms-alias=alias/redwood/evidence-signing --out=s3://forensics-us-west-2/evidence-<id>.tar.gz
6) Notify legal/compliance and set legal_hold if requested.

Roles & Responsibilities

- Security Ops: lead detection, triage, evidence collection, legal handoff readiness.
- Platform SRE: assist in containment, runbook execution, and rollback.
- Compliance: advise on retention/residency and approve evidence release.
- Engineers (owners of affected services): implement code fixes, follow remediation checklist, and create follow-up PRs.

Post-incident activities

- Post-mortem required for SEV2/SEV1 drift incidents within 5 business days. Include timeline, root cause, fixes, and evidence bundle link.
- Remediation verification: policy-as-code tests added to CI must run successfully for 3 consecutive successful runs before closure.
- Metrics to track: mean-time-to-detect (MTTD) target <= 30 minutes for high-confidence drift, mean-time-to-contain (MTTC) target <= 60 minutes.

Requesting Temporary Exception or Emergency Elevation

- Workflow summary: Exceptions to be requested in the RBAC exception tracker with justification, duration, and compensating controls (MFA required, IP allowlist, session recording). All temporary exceptions auto-expire and require manual extension.
- Evidence requirement: Exceptions must include expected audit events and a snapshot reminder to collect those events at closure.

Appendices

A: Artifact examples
- Sample evidence bundle manifest (fields listed above).
- Example CLI snippets and script headers are kept in /ops/documents/entitlement-playbook-samples/

B: Queries and detector IDs
- Detector IDs: ENT-DRIFT-001 (git-vs-runtime mismatch), ENT-DRIFT-002 (unapproved-high-priv-role), ENT-DRIFT-003 (service-account-key-usage-from-new-region).

C: Compliance mapping
- Map of regulatory retention obligations per region: US (HIPAA/contractual) up to 7y, EU (GDPR) restrict transfer—minimize cross-border artifact movements, APAC depends on contract. Compliance should be consulted for every cross-border evidence export.
